Two roads, one tuning.

Start: išartum, after 7 earlier moves. Destination: embūbum.

Initial session string 1: 440 Hz. Companion strings: octave. Sound: plucked.

Modern exact 4/3 and 3/2 realization. These numerical pitches and the comparison transposition are not recorded on the tablets.

A · Loosen (2 moves)

  1. Loosen 2 + 9kitmum
  2. Loosen 6embūbum

B · Tighten (5 moves)

  1. Tighten 5qablītum
  2. Tighten 1 + 8nīš tuḫrim
  3. Tighten 4nīd(i) qablim
  4. Tighten 7pītum
  5. Tighten 3embūbum

Same name, different pitches

Every raw B pitch is 2187/2048 times A, a shift of 113.685006 cents. The interval pattern matches exactly on all nine strings.

Listen to the comparison

Route A, then route B: nine strings; B transposed to match A on string 1.

Only the heard B is transposed, by 2048/2187. The raw B column keeps the retuned result.

Filled circle: A. Open diamond: heard B. Dashed tick: starting pitch. Every string shares one logarithmic ruler.

Text, reconstruction, calculation

The seven-name network follows the scholarly reconstruction. Mirelman (2013), figure 5, p. 52 and pp. 53–55 discusses the pattern and interpretation. Rahn (2022), paragraphs 11–16 treats the reversible network and repeated cycles; paragraph 45 explains the editorial basis of tightening terminology. The two routes' exact frequency factor and their transposed equality are deductions from this workshop's chosen 4/3 and 3/2 realization, not recovered ancient measurements.

nê’um: loosen. nasāḫum: the contextual tightening reading, in an extensively restored chapter. These are normalized lemmas, not a reconstructed ancient sentence or pronunciation.

  • Sam Mirelman · Tuning Procedures in Ancient Iraq (2013)
  • Jay Rahn · Was Mesopotamian Tuning Diatonic? A Parsimonious Answer (2022)
